Aside from the hypocrisy of Facebook being worried about security flaws (their entire operation is basically an anti-privacy system), I can't help but feel like this is a bad precedent.

It is somewhat disturbing that two out of three major browsers can cripple an entire technology/software ecosystem essentially overnight. It brings to mind the problems with "walled garden" software ecosystems, as well as calls for Windows XP to have a kill switch that Microsoft can use to permanently disable all XP installations. Given that, between TPP and its ilk, and other censorship situations (including another site), the thought that they are starting to censor software like this is very unsettling.

It also is going to encourage people who need Flash (for whatever reason) to stop updating their browsers if they need it to still function, or to otherwise bypass browser checks. Mind you, I understand the security problems with Flash, but given a system that works but is insecure, and a system that is insecure but useless, people are generally going to pick the system that is insecure but functional. Additionally browsers are coming up with bugs and security holes all the time, so it stinks faintly of the pot calling the kettle black. Doubly so, if you include whatever holes Facebook likely has.

Two suggestions that i've heard a lot:

1) Drafts. Swing by your friendly local game store that speaks MTG. They will undoubtedly have some semi-regular draft nights. It's a fun, cost-effective way to get some games in and experiment with combinations, colors, etc that you might not otherwise consider.

2) Magic 2015 Duels of the Planewalkers - $10 on steam right now. Gets you access to a load of playing options for cheap and is an easy way to learn, experiment, etc.

Jokes aside, Draft. Find a local cardshop that has an FNM (Friday Night Magic), and start making friends with the drafters that show up to it. Doesn't matter that you don't know anyone; they just want enough players to draft, so you'll be welcomed to join in. No single thing will teach you resource management and utility as fast as drafting will. Additionally, I personally think it's the single best way to buy packs when you have zero collection, as you end up with cards of similar colors and themes instead of just random chance (and it's also common courtesy for them to donate the unwanted commons/uncommons to beginners). Eventually, you can start hobbling together a casual deck or two, so that you can begin to see what kinds of singles you want to buy/trade for to flesh those out into something more playable/winnable.

Hello!

I have driven to San Diego twice from Chicago and I love it. I will be returning again next week and I will be relocating eventually. I was wondering if a list can be made that explains acronyms or anything an outsider wouldn't know. For example, what is UT or UTC?

There really isn't much to it. only a couple of communities use their initials. PB - Pacific Beach OB - Ocean Beach UTC - University Town Center (trying to claim that they are La Jolla. They are not. La Jolla is west of the 5. UTC is east of the 5 and west of the 805) TJ - Tijuana, Mexico IB - Imperial Beach
I have seen these posted on Craigslist, on papers posted on the bulletin boards at Starbucks, etc. Thanks. :-)

The UT is the Union Tribune, local news paper. Other terms I can think of... Zonies are tourists from Arizona, Pico is Pico de Gallo also known as salsa. Probably obvious but I didn't know what that was when I first got here. That's all I can think of at the moment.

You'll hear the terms North County, East County, and South Bay on occasion. The names are self-explanatory, but it's worth understanding the geographic areas that they refer to and their cultural mix as opposed to the downtown and near-downtown areas.

There are 4 climate zones in the region. The closer to the coast, the more moderate the temperatures. You could end up paying more for electricity if you're near the coast, since the utilities have variable rate pricing and allow for higher energy usage the further from the coast you are.

You'll hear about "May Gray" and "June Gloom" - basically in the late Spring / early Summer the coastal regions especially get lots of morning cloud cover. This tends to break by mid-day.

There's quite a lot of homelessness here, and it's very visible. I'm not sure what Chi-town is like, but I came here from a much poorer American city, I wasn't really prepared for how much homelessness I would see and how widespread it is. As to why, I'm not sure other than it's a very agreeable climate.

If you hear something exploding around 8:55pm, good chance those are the Sea World fireworks.

Not really an outsider thing, but the food here is amazing. Again, coming from Chicago you may be jaded on food quality, but there are some great options here that won't kill your budget. Also, the beer scene is off the fucking chain.

Again, this may vary depending on your original location, but I was impressed by how cheap and fresh the produce is here. The only thing I find wanting from the East Coast is apples. The selection here is shit for apples, but honestly everything else is pretty good. Sprouts is a great place to go for fresh produce, but not much else frankly.

That's all I can think of for now.
